audit_result.proof_trace: `deleteMember` uses `createClient()` (SSR/anon-key client) for its UPDATE mutation, but the codebase documents explicitly (server.ts L54-58, CLAUDE.md) that this client causes RLS to evaluate as `authenticated` role — silently returning 0 rows for UPDATE without an error. The `{ error }` check at L529 cannot detect this silent no-op, so the function returns `{ error: null }` while `deleted_at` remains null in the database. Every other cross-user admin mutation in this file uses `createAdminClient()` for the actual write; `deleteMember` is a clear omission of this pattern.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An admin calls `deleteMember(targetUserId)` — the SSR client's UPDATE is blocked silently by RLS (0 rows affected, no error), the function reports success, but `deleted_at` stays null, allowing the "deleted" member to continue authenticating and accessing the system.

PROP-stem-system-inv-013.text: Soft delete must set deleted_at timestamp; row must not be physically removed from database.
PROP-stem-system-inv-013.assertion: forall m: delete(m) => m.deleted_at != null AND exists(DB.members, m.id)
